text: In this lesson, you will learn how to prepare data for analysis.
After this video, you will be able to articulate the importance of data preparation, define
the objectives of data preparation, and list some activities in preparing data.
The raw data that you get directly from your sources is rarely in the format that you can
use to perform analysis on.
The goal of data preparation is to create the data that will be used for analysis.
This means cleaning the data and putting the data in the right format for analysis.
The latter generally involves selecting the appropriate features to use and transforming
the data as needed.
The data that you've acquired will likely have many problems.
An important part of data preparation is to clean the data that you have to work with
to address what are referred to as data quality issues.
There are many types of data quality issues,
including missing values, duplicate data,
inconsistent or invalid data, noise, and outliers.
The problems listed here can negatively affect
the quality of the data and compromise
the analysis process and results.
So it is very important to detect
and address these data quality issues.
Some techniques to address data quality issues include,
removing data records with missing values,
merging duplicate records,
generating a best or at most reasonable estimate
for invalid values.
We will discuss these techniques in more detail
in the next lecture.
Since the goal of this step of data preparation
is cleaning the data,
it is referred to as data cleaning or data cleansing.
After the data has been cleaned, another goal of data preparation is to get the data into the format needed for analysis.
This step is referred to by many names, data munging, data wrangling, and data preprocessing.
The two broad categories of data wrangling are feature selection and feature transformation.
Feature selection involves deciding on which features to use from the existing ones available in your data.
Features can be removed, added, or combined.
Feature transformation involves changing the format of the data in some way to reduce noise or variability or make the data easier to analyze.
Two common feature transformations are scaling the data so that all features have the same value range and reducing the dimensionality,
which is effectively the number of features of the data.
We will discuss these techniques later in this lesson.
Data preparation is a very important part of the machine learning process.
It can be a tedious process, but it is a crucial step.
If you do not spend the time and effort to create good data for the analysis,
you will not get good results, no matter how sophisticated the analysis technique you're using is.
Always remember, garbage in, garbage out.
So take the time to prepare your data if you want good analysis results.
